▸ Thought for 6s
  Considering how to best structure the comparison, I'll need to detail the...
   B-Trees vs. LSM-Trees: The Architectural Battle for Storage Engine
  Supremacy

  Every database management system, key-value store, and persistent storage
  engine fundamentally relies on an indexing mechanism to bridge the gap
  between fast, volatile RAM and slow, non-volatile block storage. For
  decades, the dominant paradigm was the B-Tree (specifically the B+ Tree),
  an in-place update data structure designed to minimize disk block reads.

  Over the last two decades, however, high-throughput web architectures,
  append-only logs, and massive distributed systems have driven the rise of
  the Log-Structured Merge-Tree (LSM-Tree). Where B-Trees prioritize
  deterministic, low-latency reads by writing data directly into fixed-size
  disk pages, LSM-Trees prioritize maximum write throughput by buffering
  incoming writes in memory and writing them out sequentially as immutable
  batches.
